scope: Consequences conditional on the written candidate's existing physical H and uniform-interval proof; no new input class or independent acceptance.
moment_boundary: For a pure state, F is PSD of trace 12 and rank at most 12. At K3(F)=8, Cauchy gives Tr(F^2)>=208/9. If equality holds simultaneously, the top three eigenvalues must all be 8/3, the remaining nine nonzero eigenvalues must all be 4/9, and the other four eigenvalues vanish. This is a necessary spectral shape, not an existence, uniqueness or equality-classification claim.
strict_moment_consequence: If the 121 H-branch spinflip condition holds and 4S+8C<64/9, then Tr(F^2)<208/9 and hence K3(F)<8. For every actual rank-three Q and physical p with 0<t=|1-p|<1, the SAME-Q erasure comparison gives R3(p)-Tr[Q Lambda_p(rho)] >= t^3(1-t)(8-K3(F))/4 > 0. The term comes solely from the T1 coefficient; the other four compared layer deficits are nonnegative. The same physical reflection used in 121 covers p>1. This is a boundary consequence of the existing H region, not an extra-family result.
other_existing_branch_boundaries: For a pure one-uniform input, the existing U-branch gap is at least (1/2)(1-t)^2 t, strict whenever 0<t<1; mixtures within that branch preserve the same gap with one fixed Q.
For a pure D_p input satisfying delta>t(sqrt(39(15-S))-5), the existing first-order inequality gives a strictly positive gap at t>0; equality at the scalar threshold is not classified.

Conditional on all of 121's unreviewed uniform-interval Hessian/remainder/far proof, each pure nonproduct input has a positive gap for 0<t<=1/200; the all-density inequality at t=0 is equality. No general mixed-state equality classification follows.
